chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from the one who mentioned him, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, who said:

When Abū Ibrāhīm (عليه السلام) passed away and Abū al-Ḥasan (عليه السلام) spoke, we feared for him because of that. So it was said to him: “You have manifested a tremendous matter, and we fear this tyrant for you.” He said: “Let him exert his utmost effort, for he has no way against me.”

key_terms.أَمْرًا عَظِيمًا: a tremendous matter, referring here to a publicly declared affair of major significance
key_terms.سَبِيلَ: a way, means, or power against

ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Riḍā (عليه السلام) respond when people feared the tyrant after he openly declared his affair?
ai.summary: This report recounts the period after the passing of Abū Ibrāhīm (عليه السلام), when Abū al-Ḥasan (عليه السلام) openly spoke regarding his position, causing concern among his companions because of the ruling tyrant. The Imam’s response expresses certainty, fearlessness, and trust that the tyrant would have no power over him beyond what Allah permits.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from the one who mentioned it, from Safwan Bin Yahya who said,

‘When Abu Ibrahim<sup>asws</sup> passed away and Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> spoke fearfully upon it (the Imamate) from that, so it was said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘You<sup>asws</sup> have manifested a great matter, and we fear upon you<sup>asws</sup> of this tyrant’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Let him strive his striving, but there would not be a way for him upon me<sup>asws</sup>’.
